newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian PM sees cooperation with Pakistan.
newsitem.headline: Indian PM sees cooperation with Pakistan.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral has written to his Pakistani counterpart, Nawaz Sharif, saying he was confident the two neighbours could reach agreement in many areas during bilateral talks despite their differences on some issues, Indian officials said on Thursday.

"Though we may not agree on all issues, we see a wide range of subjects on which we believe we can collaborate effectively," Gujral said in a letter to Sharif. "I trust that our bilateral talks will help to expand cooperation in mutually beneficial areas."

Gujral, who was responding to a letter from Sharif sent after the Indian leader assumed office on Monday, said he was glad that after a long break, the two countries had recently revived bilateral talks on all outstanding issues.
"With each of us showing a constructive and forward-looking approach, we are confident that our exchanges will be useful and lead to mutually beneficial results," Gujral said.
"I am determined not to spare any effort in this endeavour."

The new Indian prime minister said he looked forward to meeting Sharif in the Maldives next month to renew the personal contact which they established in Islamabad some years ago. The two leaders were set to meet on the fringes of a regional summit in Male scheduled for May 12 to 14.
